definition: A reported visual observation of something taken at the time to be land or permanent ice, whether or not it was later confirmed.
notes: Deliberately weak. A sighting is a report, and the record of it survives whether the thing seen existed or not.

definition: The earliest recorded sighting of any Antarctic land or ice within a stated definition and a stated body of records.
notes: Never usable without both qualifications. Most disputes about 1820 are disputes about which definition and which records are in scope.

definition: The earliest recorded sighting of continental rock or the continental land surface, as distinct from an ice shelf, ice front or offshore island.
notes: The distinction on which the Bellingshausen and Bransfield accounts most often turn.

term: ice shelf or ice front observation
definition: An observation of a permanent ice margin, which may be continental in origin but is not a sighting of land.
notes: An ice front can be evidence that land lies behind it without being a sighting of that land. The data model keeps the two as separate evidence classes.

definition: The earliest recorded instance of a person standing on Antarctic land or fast ice attached to it.
notes: A separate question again, and one where the sealing record is least reliable.

definition: A feature whose existence is supported by an independent later observation, not merely by repetition on charts.
notes: Repetition between charts is not confirmation, because charts copy one another. This is the same rule the Act II inheritance claim depends on.

definition: A term the programme uses only when quoting a source or naming a historiographical position, never as its own category.
notes: It bundles seeing, recognising, reporting and being believed, and it carries national priority arguments. The dataset has no discovery field for that reason.

definition: Land drawn because theory, cosmography or inherited authority implied it should exist, with no report behind it.
Land or ice represented on the strength of testimony that had not been independently confirmed.
notes: Maps to the evidence class 'reported_not_observed'. The distinction from conjecture is whether anyone claimed to have seen it.

definition: Coastline, islands, ice or positions directly observed by a named expedition on a stated date.
notes: Maps to the evidence class 'direct_observation'. Observation is not accuracy: an observed position can still be wrong.

definition: Observations combined, corrected and fitted into a more stable cartographic model.
notes: The 1910 ice chart is the programme's type specimen. A reconciliation is a dated act, not a neutral summary.

definition: A feature later rejected, relocated or shown to be ice, mirage, error or inherited speculation, preserved with its original claim intact.
notes: Later status and original evidence are separate fields. A ghost feature is never stored merely as an error.

definition: A position derived from celestial observation with an instrument and a timekeeper, on a stated date.
notes: Maps to the evidence class 'instrumental_fix'. Carries its own uncertainty, which is not zero.

definition: A position inferred from a previous position together with course, speed and elapsed time.
notes: Historical inference made at the time by the navigator. Its error accumulates with distance from the last fix.

definition: A position or line segment supplied by Terra Chartarum to join records the sources leave apart.
notes: Ours, not theirs. Dead reckoning is a historical act by a named navigator; interpolation is a present-day drawing decision and must never be styled as evidence.

definition: The coordinate recorded by the expedition for the loss of Endurance, as published in a named account.
notes: A calculated result with its own uncertainty, and the Coda's whole subject. It is not the ship's true position and must never be labelled as one.

definition: The seabed location of the wreck as established by the 2022 search and, where designated, by the Antarctic Treaty historic site record.
notes: Held as unresolved. Reporting seen during the audit used one set of coordinates for both terms, which is exactly the confusion this pair of definitions exists to prevent.
